Traditional Austrian Krapfen

Served at: Perchta Day (Perchtenlauf)

Makes 12-15 KrapfenPrep 45 min (plus 2 hours rising)Cook 20 min

Krapfen are delightful, fluffy doughnuts, often filled with apricot jam, that hold a special place in Alpine winter traditions. They are a beloved treat during the Rauhnächte (the twelve nights between Christmas and Epiphany) and especially for Perchta Day (Perchtenlauf), symbolizing abundance and warding off evil spirits as the community celebrates the transition from winter to the promise of spring.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk, lukewarm
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar, plus 1 teaspoon
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons (7 g) active dry yeast
  • 3 1/2 cups (420 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 2 large egg yolks
  • 1 whole large egg
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 cup (55 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • Zest of 1/2 lemon (optional)
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) rum (optional, for flavor and to reduce oil absorption)
  • 2 cups (480 g) apricot jam, strained if desired
  • 4-6 cups (1-1.5 liters) vegetable oil or lard, for deep frying
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) powdered sugar, for dusting

Method

  1. In a small bowl, combine the lukewarm milk, 1 teaspoon of granulated sugar, and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, remaining 1/4 cup granulated sugar, and salt. Make a well in the center.
  3. Pour the activated yeast mixture into the well. Add the egg yolks, whole egg, melted butter, vanilla extract, lemon zest (if using), and rum (if using).
  4. Mix with a wooden spoon or a stand mixer with a dough hook until a shaggy dough forms. Knead for 8-10 minutes until the dough is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. It should pull away from the sides of the bowl.
  5. Lightly grease a clean bowl, place the dough in it, turning once to coat. Cover with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
  6. Once risen, gently punch down the dough and turn it out onto a lightly floured surface. Roll the dough to about 1/2 inch (1.25 cm) thickness.
  7. Using a 3-inch (7.5 cm) round cutter, cut out circles. Gather the scraps, gently re-knead once, and cut out more circles. You should get 12-15 Krapfen.
  8. Place the cut Krapfen on a lightly floured baking sheet, leaving some space between them. Cover loosely with a clean kitchen towel and let them rise again in a warm place for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
  9. While the Krapfen are rising for the second time, heat the vegetable oil or lard in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven to 340-350°F (170-175°C). Use a deep-fry thermometer to monitor the temperature.
  10. Carefully place 2-3 Krapfen at a time into the hot oil, ensuring not to overcrowd the pot. Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and puffed. The Krapfen should develop a light ring around the middle.
  11. Using a slotted spoon, remove the fried Krapfen and place them on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
  12. Once slightly cooled but still warm, fill the Krapfen. You can do this by making a small incision on the side with a knife and piping in the apricot jam using a pastry bag fitted with a plain round tip, or by using a Bismark doughnut tip.
  13. Dust generously with powdered sugar before serving. Krapfen are best enjoyed fresh.

Tips

  • For the classic 'white ring' around the Krapfen, ensure your oil temperature is consistent and not too hot. Covering the pot for the first minute of frying can also help create steam for a better rise.
  • If you don't have a pastry bag, you can slice the Krapfen almost in half horizontally and spoon in the jam.
  • Experiment with other fillings like plum butter (Powidl) or vanilla cream for a delicious variation.
